subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination (FinPay)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination (FinPay)

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can coordinate the customer-led load test: 

Summary of performance targets you called out:
- 95th percentile request latency (non-streaming) for 256-token generations: <= 350 ms
- Streaming first-byte latency (time to first chunk) for conversational/streaming calls: <= 150 ms
- Sustained throughput target: 500 concurrent requests (peak bursts to 1,000)
- Tokens-per-second throughput: target ~40k tokens/s across the fleet for the workload profile you described
- SLO window: 5-minute rolling windows for latency/availability alerts

What we need from FinPay for customer-led load test:
1) Confirm test window(s) (we suggested a 2-hour window during off-peak).
2) List of static egress IPs that will run the k6/Locust workload (so we can IP allowlist).
3) Preferred endpoint to test (streaming vs non-streaming).
4) Any script artifacts you already have (k6/Locust) — we can adapt our example script.

What we’ll provide from Redwood:
- A short k6 example and loadtest instructions (attached: redwood_k6_example.js, loadtest_instructions.pdf).
- A time-limited test API key and test project (finpay_test_api_key.txt will be delivered in a follow-up email).
- IP ranges to add to your allowlist: 34.201.0.0/16 and 52.23.128.0/18 (we can add specific addresses on request).
- A recommended ramp profile: 5m ramp to 50% load, 10m steady, 5m ramp to 100% peak, 30m steady, then 10m cool-down.
- Monitoring links for live metrics and token-level cost/latency breakdowns.

Next steps (action items):
- Alex: confirm test window and provide test runner IPs (reply in thread).
- Marissa/Laura: we’ll provision a test project and generate the ephemeral API key once Alex confirms the IP list and window.
- Dylan: coordinate internal monitoring and on-call for the test window.

Thanks — I’ll hand off to Laura for the technical details and the sample script.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — that recap is perfect. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we lock a window: 

1) We will run k6 from our CI runners (static IPs available) and may also run a secondary run from k6 cloud. We can provide both IP sets — prefer your allowlist for the CI runner IPs.
2) For streaming tests: we plan to exercise both streaming (SSE) and non-streaming endpoints. For streaming, is there any guidance on client-side chunk interval or max keep-alive?
3) Regarding the tokens/s metric — we’ll translate our prompt mix into token estimates and aim for the 40k tokens/s target total. Any guidance on concurrency vs. tokens trade-offs would help.

Proposed test window: Thu Mar 5, 02:00–04:00 UTC (our off-peak). Will that work for you?

Attaching our draft k6 script (we’ll also share the CI egress IPs in a follow-up).

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering — FinPay

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination (FinPay)

Alex — thanks, quick tech notes and what we’ll provision: 

Technical guidance (short):
- Streaming: use Server-Sent Events (SSE) or chunked HTTP response. Client should allow a ~60s idle keep-alive for long responses; we send chunks at generation boundaries. Aim to assert time-to-first-chunk < 150 ms.
- Non-streaming: target median latency ~120–180 ms; 95th < 350 ms for 256-token responses per your target.
- Concurrency vs tokens: if you increase concurrency, per-request latency may increase due to batching trade-offs. For a token-heavy mix, prioritize fewer concurrent requests with larger token payloads to measure per-token throughput; for many short chats, simulate higher QPS with smaller tokens.
- Suggested ramp: identical to Dylan’s suggestion but we recommend an additional sanity warm-up: 10m at 10% before the formal ramp.

Provisioning from Redwood (I’ll action once Dylan confirms window and Alex provides IPs):
- Test project: finpay-loadtest (read-only observability access provided).
- Ephemeral API key: expires in 7 days (will send finpay_test_api_key.txt).
- Allowlist ranges to add if you prefer CIDR: 34.201.0.0/16 and 52.23.128.0/18. If you provide exact runner IPs we’ll add them to the project allowlist immediately.

Attachments included here: redwood_k6_example.js — an example k6 script with streaming and non-streaming scenarios; loadtest_instructions.pdf — checklist and recommended Grafana dashboards.

If the Thu Mar 5 02:00–04:00 UTC window works, we’ll provision the project tonight and send the API key tomorrow morning. Also cc’ing Marissa to schedule an internal on-call and Slack channel for the run.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination (FinPay)

Laura — Thu Mar 5 02:00–04:00 UTC works for us. CI egress IPs (primary runners): 3.225.45.12, 3.225.45.13, 3.225.45.14. We will also kick off a k6 cloud run from cloud IPs (we’ll share those soon).

We reviewed your k6 example and made small tweaks to our draft. We will run the following profile:
- 10m warm-up at 10%
- 5m ramp to 50%
- 10m steady at 50%
- 5m ramp to 100%
- 30m steady at peak
- 10m cool-down

One last ask: can you set a timeout on the Redwood side to 90s for these test requests (we sometimes get longer tails during peak generation)? If you prefer we can keep client-side timeouts and retry behavior controlled on our side.

We’ll start the run at 02:00 UTC Thursday and share results afterwards.

— Alex

— Dylan
